record.paper_title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
record.original_question: For the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method and its related quadratic regularization variant for nonsmooth regularized optimization, can one develop implementations and convergence or complexity analyses that remain valid when function values, gradients, and proximal-operator evaluations are computed inexactly rather than exactly?

evidence.quote: inexact function, gradient, and proximal operator evaluations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonsmooth regularized optimization problem
    minimize_{x ∈ R^n}  f(x) + h(x),
where f : R^n → R is continuously differentiable (possibly nonconvex) with Lipschitz-continuous gradient, and h : R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is proper, lower semi-continuous, and possibly nonsmooth and nonconvex. A proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method generates iterates x_k by approximately solving, at each step, a trust-region subproblem of the form
    minimize_{s : ||s|| ≤ Δ_k}  ⟨∇f(x_k), s⟩ + (1/2)⟨s, B_k s⟩ + h(x_k + s),
where B_k is a quasi-Newton approximation to the Hessian of f and Δ_k > 0 is the trust-region radius; an associated quadratic regularization variant replaces the trust-region constraint by a quadratic penalty term (σ_k/2)||s||^2. The standard analyses of such methods assume that the objective values f(x_k), gradients ∇f(x_k), and the proximal-operator evaluations used to solve the subproblems are computed exactly.

Problem: Design implementations of the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method and of its quadratic regularization variant in which the function values f(x_k), gradients ∇f(x_k), and proximal operator evaluations are computed only inexactly, subject to controllable accuracy conditions; and establish global convergence to first-order stationary points together with worst-case iteration/evaluation complexity bounds (such as O(ε^{-2}) for reaching an ε-approximate first-order stationary point) for these inexact variants, matching those obtainable under exact evaluations.
artifact.status_search_result: A companion line of work develops a proximal trust-region method for nonsmooth optimization that permits and systematically controls inexact function and gradient evaluations, with global convergence to first-order stationary points and O(ε^{-2}) worst-case complexity, showing that inexactness (including in proximal operators) does not degrade asymptotic complexity. This addresses the inexact-evaluation extension, though the quasi-Newton trust-region variant with all three sources of inexactness combined has been treated primarily in the convex-h, smooth-f setting; a fully general treatment matching the original nonconvex regularized framework appears partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: A proximal trust-region method for nonsmooth optimization with inexact function and gradient evaluations
status_evidence.snippet: A trust-region method that permits and systematically controls the use of inexact objective function and derivative evaluations; global convergence proven; inexact proximal Newton-type variant included.
status_evidence.claim: Inexact evaluations have been incorporated and analyzed in a closely related proximal trust-region framework with matching complexity.

status_evidence.title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method for sum of smooth nonconvex f and nonsmooth (possibly nonconvex) h; analysis assumes exact evaluations.
status_evidence.claim: The original quasi-Newton trust-region analysis is under exact evaluations, motivating the inexact extension.
